g.text: One book: a scanned PDF goes in; two English PDFs and a review report come out. Every step runs in the fmt-translator Docker container;
the two models run on a local GPU or on a GPU system on the LAN (see "Where the models run"). run_full_pipeline.sh runs the steps in order.

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(246, 248, 250), rgb(23, 25, 27)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(89, 99, 110), rgb(146, 155, 164));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(9, 105, 218), rgb(86, 168, 255));
fill: light-dark(rgb(9, 105, 218), rgb(86, 168, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(9, 105, 218), rgb(86, 168, 255));

g.text: most of the run: ~5-10 s per page
Render each page at 300 dpi, resize to 1288 px (the size olmOCR-2 requires) and send
it to the vision model with vlm_ocr_prompt.txt.
The model returns four fields per page: PAGE_NUMBER, HEADER (running header),
BODY_TEXT (the text, including the author's footnotes), and FIGURES (plates / insets
Save the untouched replies to raw_ocr.txt – always, before any cleanup. Progress is
saved after every page, so an interrupted run resumes.
The layout detector finds running headers and margin (shoulder) notes on each page
image; the vision model then reads each margin note from a crop.
Clean up across the whole book: strip running headers and catchwords that leaked into
the body, make running headers consistent, place margin notes by their paragraph,
Work out page numbers from the sequence of folios read (roman front matter, plates
unnumbered) – shown only when printed or forced by the neighbours, never guessed.
Apply the reviewer's page decisions from the overrides file.
detector, CPU only, ~0.5 s per page

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(89, 99, 110), rgb(146, 155, 164)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(89, 99, 110), rgb(146, 155, 164));

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 255, 255), rgb(18, 18, 18)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(26, 127, 55), rgb(87, 174, 112));
fill: light-dark(rgb(26, 127, 55), rgb(87, 174, 112)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(26, 127, 55), rgb(87, 174, 112));

g.text: Per page: clean the step-1 text, replace tables with a [[TABLE]] marker (the PDFs
show the scan instead), skip blank and marker pages.
Translate with translation_prompt.txt plus the book's own glossary ([terms] in the
Enforce the term policy: terms English fencing literature keeps stay French and
italic (riposte, quarte); ordinary terms get their English name (parade → parry);
hard terms (coupé) are translated and footnoted once per book.
Move the author's own numbered footnotes out of the body into a footnote area,
joining one that continues onto the next page.
Check every answer – refusal, non-Latin script, not English, all capitals, too short,
a lost margin note – and retry up to 3 times, later tries hotter and with a stricter
Never drop a page: keep the best failed try flagged [low-confidence translation —
review], or the original text flagged [translation unavailable].
Then translate figure captions and running headers, and apply the overrides file's
Later runs retranslate only the pages whose extracted text changed (per-page
Python rules after each answer: kept

g.text: Left: the original scan page, unchanged.
Right: the translation with its running header and page number. Where the scan has
a text layer, each paragraph starts level with its source paragraph.
Text shrinks 9 → 8 → 7 pt to fit, then continues on a "(cont.)" page – never cut

g.text: You: check the listed pages against the facing scan → record each decision in books/<stem>.overrides.toml
→ apply_overrides.py (no model) → rebuild the PDFs. Steps 1 and 2 re-apply the file on every run,
so a decision is made once and survives any regeneration.

g.text: local – both models run on a GPU in the same system, through a llama.cpp build
inside the image. Each step starts its own llama-server and stops it when done, so
only one model is in VRAM at a time.
remote – the models run on another GPU system on the LAN behind llama-swap (port
11500, bearer token), which loads the vision or text model per request. This host
